answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume, no buffer, and only 14 days to expiry, switching primary vendor (memory_c2) carries real delivery risk despite its cost win — onboarding was quick last year but that was without a capacity-constrained line. Negotiating terms with the incumbent targets the 18% mandate through price and payment-term movement (memory_c4) and potentially multi-year volume pricing (memory_c6), while preserving the stable integration and uninterrupted deliveries recorded in memory_c1. I am verifying c4 and c6 to confirm the magnitude and conditions of those negotiated savings before committing, since the size of the achievable cut determines whether negotiation alone can approach the 18% target or whether a switch must be reconsidered next cycle. Confidence is moderate pending archive confirmation.
